decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approaches to the two cameras; reserve middle basket for cameras, left for figures, right for pens. Gripper-to-link offset still estimated.
Advance each open gripper above its camera while pitching downward; keep separate workspaces and inspect before closing.
Make final camera alignment, close both grippers, and lift slightly to inspect retention. Right camera appears farther ahead in wrist view.
Both cameras appear between the fingers. Lift clear of the figures and move toward separate left/right portions of the middle basket, maintaining closure.
Carry retained cameras over left and right halves of the blue basket, lowering only after clearing its front rim.
Lower the cameras into the blue basket, open both grippers, then retreat upward and outward to inspect settling.
Withdraw from blue basket. Approach the white figure with the left arm and the white pen with the right, rotating the right gripper across the pen.
Descend cautiously around the white figure and across the white pen; both cameras are visibly settled in the blue basket.
Close around the white figure and white pen, then lift vertically to check retention before transferring them.
The lift did not visibly retain the figure or pen. Reopen and descend farther in small increments, correcting the estimated link-to-contact height.
Recenter on the figure's head and close at the deeper grasp height. Relieve right table contact slightly, close on the pen, and lift both with a small lateral check.
Both objects now remain visibly between the fingers during lifting. Raise clear of the basket rims and carry the figure leftward and pen toward the red basket.
Replan from interrupted prefix: use smaller forward increments combined with lowering to preserve elbow-up continuity. Keep both retained objects closed over their assigned baskets.
Release the white figure into the left basket and the white pen into the red basket, then lift and retreat to inspect settling.
Both released objects are visibly inside their baskets. Approach the remaining gray figure and black pen; turn the right gripper across the black pen's axis.
Refine alignment from the wrist views and descend with open grippers toward the gray figure's head and the black pen.
Descend the final few centimeters, close on the gray figure and black pen, and lift gently to verify retention in RGB.
Lift the retained gray figure and black pen clear, moving toward the white and red baskets respectively while keeping elbow-up configuration and grippers closed.
Gray figure is retained; position it in the left basket. Black pen remained on the table, so reopen the right gripper and return above it for a deeper centered grasp.
Lower and release the gray figure into the white basket. Descend the right gripper around the black pen to a deeper contact height before closing.
Both figures are inside the left basket. Withdraw the left arm while closing the right gripper at the deeper black-pen grasp height, then lift and shift slightly to test retention visually.
Black pen remains between the fingers during the lift. Carry it toward the red basket, keeping closed, while gradually returning the left arm toward its origin.
Finish the left arm's gradual return to origin while lowering the retained black pen over the red basket interior.
Open the right gripper to release the black pen into the red basket, pause for settling, then withdraw upward/backward. Fine-align the left arm at origin.
All six objects are visibly in their category baskets. Return the open right arm toward origin gradually, keeping elbow-up continuity; the left arm remains at origin.
Complete the open right arm's return to origin with tapering increments. Keep all baskets untouched while the sorted objects settle.
